subject: Cooking
title: Marinades: Myth vs. Science
description: A 60-second lesson on Marinades: Myth vs. Science.

hook.text: Recipes say to marinate chicken overnight for deep flavor. Science says it barely penetrates 2mm.

buildup.text: Marinade molecules are too large to move deep into dense muscle tissue quickly.

discovery.text: Acid in marinades denatures surface proteins, changing texture — but doesn't 'infuse' flavor deeply.

twist.text: Too much acid or time makes the surface mushy. Over-marinated fish turns chalky, like ceviche.

climax.text: Salt is the exception — it's tiny enough to penetrate deeply. Brining works; marinades mostly don't.

punchline.text: Marinades flavor the surface. Salt flavors the whole.

quiz.question: Why do most marinades fail to deeply flavor meat?
options: Molecules are too large to penetrate

details.summary: Marinades add surface flavor but penetrate only a few millimeters into meat, not the deep interior as commonly believed. Acids in marinades denature surface proteins, changing texture rather than tenderizing deeply.
details.whyItMatters: Knowing marinades' actual limitations prevents wasted time and ruined textures. Surface flavor is valuable, but expecting deep penetration from a marinade leads to disappointment.
takeaways: Marinades penetrate only 1 to 3 millimeters into meat
Acid denatures surface proteins rather than tenderizing deeply
Enzymatic marinades with kiwi or pineapple work faster

faq.question: If marinades barely penetrate, why do chefs use them?
faq.answer: Surface flavor is significant because we taste the exterior first. Marinades also affect texture and browning. Oil-based marinades conduct heat better for improved Maillard reactions. The key is realistic expectations — marinades season the surface, not the center.

faq.question: Can you over-marinate meat?
faq.answer: Yes. Extended acid exposure turns the surface mushy and gray as proteins break down excessively. Fish and shrimp can over-marinate in under an hour. Chicken becomes chalky after 24 hours in acidic marinades. Follow recommended times for the best texture.
